records.title: A Shifted-Golomb Identity for the Full-Memory Prefix of Run-Constructed Almost Golomb Sequences

evidence.excerpt:
Golomb's self-describing sequence $G$ is the unique nondecreasing sequence
of positive integers in which the value $m$ occurs exactly $G(m)$ times
\cite{Golomb1966}.  Cloitre introduced finite-memory analogues by replacing
the full cumulative sum with a sliding window of length $r$ and selecting an
earliest monotone solution \cite{Cloitre2026Almost}.  If $a_r(k)=0$ for
$k\leq0$, the implicit equation is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:implicit}
 a_r\!\left(\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}a_r(n-j)\right)=n.
\end{equation}
The source conjectures that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:source-conjecture}
 a_r(r)=G(r-1)\qquad(r\geq3)
\end{equation}
and reports a computational verification for $r\leq200$
\cite[Conjecture~9.3]{Cloitre2026Almost}.

For the sets $\RV_{\ell,k}$ and $\TC_{\ell,k}$ of networks with $\ell$ leaves
and $k$ reticulations, put
\[
 \Delta_k(\ell)=|\RV_{\ell,k}|-|\TC_{\ell,k}|.
\]
Batle's Conjecture~5.1 \cite{Batle2026} asserts, for $\ell\ge k+1$, that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:conjecture}
 \Delta_k(\ell)=A_k(\ell)(2\ell-3)!!
 -B_k(\ell)2^{\ell-k+1}\ell!,
\end{equation}
where $A_k,B_k$ are polynomials of degrees $2k-1$ and $2k-3$, respectively,
and the leading coefficient of $A_k$ is $2^k$.  The cases $k=2,3$ motivated
the conjecture; the case $k=4$ was explicitly left open.

records.title: The sharp variation constant for the centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator on P₁₁
records.reason: 只引用、证明/否定或局部处理已有猜想/问题，未正式提出作者新猜想。

evidence.excerpt:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite connected undirected graph.  The centered graph
Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator averages the absolute value of a function
over graph-distance balls.  Liu and Xue studied sharp variation constants for
this operator on finite graphs~\cite{LiuXue2021}.  González-Riquelme, Kovač,
and Madrid subsequently determined further sharp constants and posed the
path-graph conjecture~\cite[Conjecture~5]{GKM2026}:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:path-conjecture}
  \Cpath n=1-\frac1n\qquad(n\geq3).
\end{equation}
Their paper proves the case $P_4$ by finite linear programming and reports
numerical evidence through $n=10$~\cite[Section~3.2 and Conjecture~5]{GKM2026}.

evidence.excerpt:
Let $\beta_d>1$ be the Perron root of $X^d-X-1$.  Akiyama proved that
$\beta_d$ is non-Parry for every $d\geq 4$~\cite[Theorem~1.1]{Akiyama2016}.

Their Table~3.3 labels the cases $4\leq d\leq 10$ as non-Parry for all positive
powers, while the surrounding text describes the table as numerical support
and reports computations through $d=100$~\cite[Table~3.3 and
Remark~3.4]{HareHichri2026}.  The exact finite witnesses behind the $d=4$ row
are not supplied there.

Write the two-variable Links--Gould invariant in Ishii's normalization as
\[
  \LG(K;t_0,t_1)=\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}t_0^it_1^j.

\section{Introduction}
For a finite simple graph $G$, let $\chi(G)$ and $\crn(G)$ denote its chromatic
and crossing numbers. Albertson's conjecture asserts
\[
 \chi(G)\geq r\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\crn(G)\geq\crn(K_r).

verification through 12 at that time~\cite{Albertson_Cranston_Fox_2009}.
Cranston recently proved it

48 vertices~\cite{cranston2025progressalbertsonsconjecture}.

\section{Introduction}
Let $S_{d,n}$ be the $d$-skeleton of the $(n-1)$-simplex. Thus its facets are the $(d+1)$-subsets of $[n]$. The cases $d\leq2$ and $d\geq n-3$ are known; see \cite{Bigdeli2019,Culbertson2020,Coleman2022} and the references therein. Consequently $(n,d)=(7,3)$ is the first parameter pair outside those ranges.

records.reason: 只引用、证明/否定或局部处理已有猜想/问题，未正式提出作者新猜想。

evidence.excerpt:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph.  A \emph{bond partition} of $G$ is
a set partition of $V$ whose blocks induce connected subgraphs.  Write
$\Pi_G$ for the set of bond partitions.  We use the multiweighted-bond
symmetric function $\Psi_G\in\Sym$ and the M\"obius symmetric function $M_H$
of Gonz\'alez D'Le\'on and Wachs~\cite{gonzalez-wachs2026}.  Put
\[
  F_{G,d}=\Psi_G|_{\deg d},\qquad
  L_{G,d}=F_{G,d}^2-F_{G,d-1}F_{G,d+1}.
\]
The Schur-log-concavity conjecture in~\cite[Conjecture~7.3]{gonzalez-wachs2026}
asserts that $L_{G,d}$ is Schur-positive for every graph and every $d$.
It refines the ordinary chromatic-polynomial log-concavity proved by
Huh~\cite{huh2012}.

records.title: The Optimal High-SNR Leading Coefficient for Seven Spherical Codewords in Four Dimensions
records.reason: 只引用、证明/否定或局部处理已有猜想/问题，未正式提出作者新猜想。

evidence.excerpt:
High-SNR error asymptotics for fixed multidimensional constellations are
governed by nearest-neighbor geometry~\cite{AlvaradoAgrellBrannstrom2018}.
Zlatanov introduced the SNR-wise optimized leading coefficient
$K^*_{M,n}$ and characterized it through the limiting minimum of a Gaussian
soft-packing energy~\cite{Zlatanov2026}.  In dimension $n=4$ the exponent in
that energy is exactly the exponent in~\eqref{eq:objective}.  For the
orthoplex range $M=n+k$, the same work proves
\[
 K^*_{n+k,n}\le 4k(k-1)
\]
by an SNR-dependent construction and conjectures equality when
$n\ge4$ and $3\le k\le n-1$.  Thus $(n,k)=(4,3)$ is the smallest instance:
the cited construction gives $K^*_{7,4}\le24$, whereas the missing direction
is a global lower bound over all SNR-dependent families.  Our contribution is
that converse for this one instance.  This comparison is limited to the cited
literature and is not a broader priority claim.

records.title: Exact Determination of r(9) for Permutation Crossword Grids
records.reason: 只引用、证明/否定或局部处理已有猜想/问题，未正式提出作者新猜想。

evidence.excerpt:
For $w\in S_n$, let $\Grid(w)$ be the $n\times n$ array in which square
$(i,j)$ is black exactly when $j=w(i)$.  An \emph{across word} is a maximal
nonempty contiguous run of white squares in a row; a \emph{down word} is
defined analogously in a column.  A complete non-attacking rook placement is
a set of white squares meeting every across word and every down word exactly
once.  Write $\RP(G)$ for the set of these placements and
\[
  r(n)=\max_{w\in S_n}|\RP(\Grid(w))|.
\]
These definitions and the maximization question are due to Lewis and
Won~\cite{LewisWon2026}.  They computed
\[
  r(1),\ldots,r(8)=1,1,1,5,17,73,469,3493
\]
and conjectured that a maximizer is always layered of shape
$(m,1,\ldots,1,m)$ for a suitable $m$.

evidence.excerpt:
Brenti's 1995 article developed the broader systematic connection between
combinatorics and total positivity \cite{Brenti1995}.  The conjecture that the
Eulerian triangle is totally positive was formulated in Brenti's 1996 chapter

including strict positivity of all admissible minors of orders at most three

order-four problem to 126 minors, while explicitly withholding a proof because
that computation had not been independently verified
\cite[Remark~1.2]{Mao2026}.  Our contribution is an exhaustive reconstruction
of those 126 parameter templates together with exact universal sign
certificates.  The closest inspected work is Mao's preprint; this comparison is
bounded and makes no broader priority claim.

records.reason: 只引用、证明/否定或局部处理已有猜想/问题，未正式提出作者新猜想。

evidence.excerpt:
Erickson posed the transversal achievement game for an $n\times n$ grid
\cite{Erickson2010}.  A transversal contains one cell in every row and every
column.  Ranđelović proved that the first player wins for $n\geq4$
\cite{Randjelovic2025}.  Guan subsequently gave a fully specified strategy
that wins by ply $2n+3$ for every $n\geq4$ \cite{Guan2026}.  For $n=4$ this
gives an upper bound of $11$ plies.  Guan's exhaustive search shows that this
bound is attained against that particular strategy for $n=4,5,6$, and
Conjecture~14 of \cite{Guan2026} proposes that $2n+3$ is the optimal-play
length.  As emphasized there, checking the replies to one X strategy does not
exclude a different, faster X strategy.

records.reason: 只引用、证明/否定或局部处理已有猜想/问题，未正式提出作者新猜想。

\begin{abstract}
For $m\geq6$, let $J_m$ be obtained by stacking a vertex $w$ in one
face $pr_0r_1$ of the bipyramid over an $m$-cycle.  An edge is called
identifying when its unlabeled edge-deleted card has no nonisomorphic
maximal-planar parent.  We prove that the identifying edges of $J_m$ are
exactly
\[
  pw,\qquad wr_0,\qquad wr_1.
\]
The full automorphism group has order two, and these edges form the two
orbits $\{pw\}$ and $\{wr_0,wr_1\}$.  Thus there are three identifying
edges, and their two card types have full-deck multiplicities one and two.
We also determine every edge orbit and give an explicit nonisomorphic
maximal-planar completion for every remaining orbit.  This completes a
proposed classification within the family; it is not presented as an
author-declared open problem from the preceding literature.
\end{abstract}

records.title: A Modulo-Five Congruence for Overcolored Partition 4-Tuples Restricted by Parity of the Parts
records.reason: 只引用、证明/否定或局部处理已有猜想/问题，未正式提出作者新猜想。

evidence.excerpt:
For $j\geq1$, put
\[
 f_j=(q^j;q^j)_\infty=\prod_{m\geq1}(1-q^{jm}).
\]
The overcolored partition $k$-tuples restricted by parity studied by
Thejitha and Fathima have generating function
\begin{equation}\label{eq:general-gf}
 \sum_{N\geq0}\bar b^k_{r,s}(N)q^N
 =\frac{f_2^{(3s-2r)k}}{f_1^{2sk}f_4^{(s-r)k}}.
\end{equation}
Their Conjecture~7.1 records several congruences supported there by
computation~\cite{ThejithaFathima2026}.  The specialization
$(r,s,k)=(4,2,4)$ in \eqref{eq:general-gf} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:F}
 F(q):=\frac{f_4^8}{f_1^{16}f_2^8}
      =\sum_{N\geq0}a(N)q^N,
 \qquad a(N)=\bar b^4_{4,2}(N).
\end{equation}
Related generating-function congruences for the overcubic specialization
were obtained by Chac\'on and Sellers~\cite{ChaconSellers2026}; their
families do not contain the specialization in \eqref{eq:F}.

\begin{abstract}
Let $p\in\F_2[t]$ be any irreducible polynomial of degree $n\geq 3$,
let $J_n$ denote inversion in $\F_2[t]/(p)$ in the associated polynomial
basis (with $0^{-1}=0$), and regard the entries of

\[
        f_{\rm raw}(P,u)=\adj(P)J_n(Pu),
\]
including singular $P$, we prove

top-degree ANF coefficient.  Its value is an off-diagonal entry of the
inverse trace Gram matrix, while its matrix-variable support is a disjoint
edge together with an alternating spanning path.  This closes the
algebraic-degree half of a two-part question posed by Zhang and Zhang.  It
does not prove the conjectured value of the joint ANF leap, so the original
two-part problem remains unresolved.

records.title: A Conjectural Unary-Theta Formula for the 6n+1-Section of 18-Colored Generalized Frobenius Partitions
records.reason: 作者以 Our proposed refinement 和显式 Conjecture 提出新的逐系数模16一元 theta 同余，覆盖整个6n+1截面；正文区分其与 Das–Nath–Sarma 的两条已有同余猜想并明确未证。

evidence.excerpt:
\begin{abstract}
Das, Nath, and Sarma recently conjectured two congruences modulo $16$ for
the $18$-colored generalized Frobenius partition function.  We propose the
stronger, explicitly unproved, coefficientwise congruence
\[
 \sum_{m\geq0}\cphi_{18}(6m+1)q^m
 \equiv 4\frac{f_2f_3^2}{f_1f_6}
 =4\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}q^{k(3k-1)/2}\quad(\mathrm{mod}\ 16),
 \qquad f_d=(q^d;q^d)_\infty.
\]
We prove the equality between the two expressions on the right and show that
the proposed congruence would imply both source congruences.  Exact
computations from two different generating descriptions support it for
$0\leq m\leq504$; the range $0\leq m\leq99$ was used for discovery and
$100\leq m\leq504$ was held out.  A termwise dissection audit gives several
formal parity cancellations but leaves other grouped cancellations unproved.

All congruences of power series below are coefficientwise.  Our proposed
refinement is the following.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Conjecture.}
In \((\mathbb Z/16\mathbb Z)[[q]]\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:main-conj}
 H(q)\equiv4\frac{f_2f_3^2}{f_1f_6}\quad(\mathrm{mod}\ 16).
\end{equation}
The quotient is well defined as a formal power series because every $f_d$
has constant coefficient one.  The conjecture is stronger than
\eqref{eq:source-conj}: it predicts every coefficient in the entire
$6n+1$ section modulo $16$, rather than only two residue classes within
that section.  A bounded search of the cited sources and exact formula
searches through September 7, 2026, located no source stating
\eqref{eq:main-conj}; this is a description of the search, not a priority
claim.

\cite[Definition~3.3]{BaolahyBenjamin2026}, equal rows of a fixed length are
rotated diagonally by one cyclic factor, and positive closure is proved for

Jeffries~\cite{Jeffries2026} introduced the following multi-tournament
parameter.  For integers $m,k\geq1$, let $f(m,k)$ be the least integer
$n\geq k+1$ for which there are tournaments $T_1,\ldots,T_m$ on one
$n$-element set $V$ satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{eq:property}
  \forall U\in\binom{V}{k}\quad
  \exists i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\quad
  \exists x\in V\setminus U\quad
  \forall u\in U,\quad x\to_{T_i}u.
\end{equation}
Thus the same outside vertex, in the same tournament, must beat every
member of $U$.  Proposition~2.3 and Theorem~2.2 of
Jeffries~\cite{Jeffries2026} give the upper bound in the theorem below,
and the table there reports equality on this parameter slice for
$k=3,4,5,6$ using a SAT formulation.  The source notes that general
nontrivial lower bounds for $f(m,k)$ are absent, but it does not present
this slice as a numbered open problem; no claim of publication priority is
made here.

evidence.excerpt:
Chen and Selover establish universal linear positivity in their
Theorem~4.10, formulate positivity of the available higher residue
coefficients in Conjecture~4.1, and discuss the quadratic calculation in
Section~5 of \cite{ChenSelover2026}. Theorem~\ref{thm:main} settles the
quadratic case for the full prime-power domain. Its additional ingredient
